```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

```{r}
library(adempR)
```

Long simulations are interrupted: laptops sleep, cluster jobs hit their
time limit, a method hangs. adempR records progress so that no work is
lost and none is counted twice.

## The run directory

```{r}
study <- sim_study("recovery",
  scenarios = sim_scenarios(n = c(20L, 50L)),
  generate = function(scenario, context) rexp(scenario$n),
  estimands = list(sim_estimand("mean", sim_truth_exact(function(scenario) 1))),
  methods = list(mean = function(data) sim_estimate("mean", mean(data)),
                 median_scaled = function(data) sim_estimate("mean", median(data) / log(2))),
  retention = sim_retention(data = TRUE))
path <- file.path(tempdir(), "recovery-run")
run <- sim_run(study, replications = 40, seed = 5, path = path, chunk_size = 10)
list.files(path)
```

* `manifest.rds` and `manifest.json` record the study fingerprints, the
  seed, the stream registry, the environment (R and package versions; no
  host or user names) and the revision history.
* `batches/` holds committed chunks. Each is written to a temporary file,
  a checksum sidecar is written, and both are renamed into place; the
  rename of the sidecar is the commit point.
* `artifacts/` holds retained data sets and fits.
* `quarantine/` receives corrupt or orphaned files.
* `LOCK/` exists while a coordinator is running.

## Interrupting and resuming

Call `sim_run()` again with the same study and seed. Committed tasks are
skipped; only missing ones run. `sim_resume(path)` does the same from the
manifest alone.

```{r}
run <- sim_run(study, replications = 60, seed = 5, path = path, chunk_size = 10)
run
```

The tests kill R with `SIGKILL` at each stage of a commit (after the data
file is written, before the sidecar, after the commit) and check that the
resumed run equals an uninterrupted one. If a run died holding the lock,
the next run on the same host detects that the process is gone and takes
over the lock. A lock held on another host must be released with
`sim_unlock()` after checking that no process is running.

## Corruption and duplicates

A batch whose checksum does not match is reported as corrupt and ignored
when reading. The next `sim_run()` moves it to `quarantine/` and reruns its
tasks. If the same task is committed twice (for example by two workers
after a network partition), identical copies are deduplicated; copies
whose scientific columns differ stop with a conflict error, because one of
them must be wrong. Timing columns are not compared.

## Changing the study

The run directory records fingerprints of each part of the study, and
`sim_run()` compares them with the study it is given:

* A different data-generating mechanism is an error: use a new directory.
* Added scenarios and methods are run. Removed scenarios and methods keep
  their committed results on disk, but summaries leave them out.
* A changed method requires `update = TRUE`. Only that method is refit;
  others keep their results.
* A changed truth, estimand metadata, measure set or failure policy is
  applied at evaluation with no refitting.
* A changed `timeout` or number of `retries` applies to new work only.
  Committed fits keep the settings they ran with; `retry_failed = TRUE`
  reruns fits that failed under the old settings.
* Requesting fewer replications than the directory holds gives a warning;
  all committed replications are kept and summarized.

Fingerprints are built from the deparsed code of each function and the
values of the free variables it uses (and from `depends`, for anything the
code reaches indirectly), never from serialized bytecode.

Each of these changes is recorded as a revision in the manifest:

```{r}
study2 <- sim_amend(study, measures = sim_measures("bias", "mse", "mae"),
                    reason = "add MAE")
run <- sim_run(study2, replications = 60, seed = 5, path = path)
vapply(run$manifest$revisions, function(r) paste(r$changes, collapse = "; "), "")
```

## Replay

`sim_replay()` recomputes one replication from the recorded streams and
compares the result with the stored one. With retained data it also
checks that the regenerated data set is identical.

```{r}
rp <- sim_replay(run, scenario = 2, replication = 33)
rp$matches
rp$data_matches
head(rp$data)
```

This is the fastest way to debug a failure: find the replication in
`sim_results(run)$attempts`, replay it, and step through the method with
the exact data it saw.

## Parallel execution

With `backend = "future"` chunks are evaluated by `future.apply` workers
and committed by the coordinator. Results are identical to the sequential
backend.

```{r, eval = FALSE}
future::plan(future::multisession, workers = 4)
run <- sim_run(study, replications = 1000, seed = 5, path = path, backend = "future")
```

or pass `workers = 4` to use a temporary multisession plan. Workers load
the installed adempR and the packages listed in the study's `packages`
fields.
